Chapter 4: The Existence of God—Securing the Foundation of Knowledge.
Now that we've established the self as a thinking being, there’s a new hurdle to face—how do we actually trust what we know? If our minds can make mistakes, how can we be sure our reasoning is solid?
To tackle this, let’s turn to one of the biggest questions out there: does God exist?
Here’s where the journey really gets interesting. Think about the idea of God—a being who’s all-powerful, all-knowing, and perfectly good. That’s not an idea you just dream up out of thin air, especially if you’re a limited, imperfect person. It’s a bit like picturing a perfect circle without ever having seen anything flawless. The thought of absolute perfection has to come from something... or someone... that’s truly perfect.
Following this line of reasoning, you reach a pretty profound conclusion: God exists, and God is the source of our idea of perfection. But it doesn’t stop there—if God is truly perfect, then God isn’t out to deceive us. A perfect being wouldn’t create minds that are constantly being tricked or misled.
So what does that mean for us? It means when we have those moments where our ideas feel crystal clear and distinct, we can actually trust them. They’re not just random thoughts—they’re gifts from a creator who’s both good and trustworthy.
Think of it like hiring an architect to build your house. If you know that architect is both talented and honest, you can trust the house will be sturdy. In the same way, if God is perfect and not a deceiver, then your mind—especially when it’s working with clarity—can be trusted too.
Of course, this doesn’t mean we never make mistakes. We still slip up, especially when we rush or don’t have all the facts. But when we slow down and focus on what’s clear and distinct, we can be confident in what we discover.
So, here’s the key takeaway: the existence of God acts like a safety net for our knowledge. Without that assurance, even our most careful thinking could come undone. But with it, we’re free to build a system of knowledge that’s not just solid, but also wide-reaching.
This step is more than just another argument—it changes the whole game. Suddenly, searching for certainty isn’t a lonely journey. It’s a partnership, supported by the very nature of reality itself.
